content.text:
## Investigation summary

**One root cause, a connectivity failure between `ts-route-plan-service` and `ts-travel2-service`.** The fault is on that call path. I found no sign of a fault inside `ts-travel2-service` itself. The telemetry shows where the failure occurs, but not the underlying network mechanism (DNS, endpoints, network policy, or connection-pool behaviour), so that still needs confirming on the cluster.

### Affected endpoints
Abnormal-window traces against normal baseline:

| Service / endpoint | Abnormal | Normal |
|---|---|---|
| `ts-ui-dashboard` (user-facing, `/travelPlan/*`) | avg ~612 ms, p95 ~136 ms | avg ~87 ms, p95 ~241 ms |
| `ts-travel-plan-service` `/travelPlan/cheapest`, `/minStation`, `/quickest` | avg 87 s, p95 131 s, 24 HTTP 5xx | avg 243 ms, no 5xx |
| `ts-route-plan-service` `/routePlan/cheapestRoute`, `/minStopStations`, `/quickestRoute` | avg 59 s, p95 131 s, 12 HTTP 5xx | avg 232 ms, no 5xx |

Unaffected: `ts-travel2-service` direct calls from `ui-dashboard` (`trips/left`, ~77 ms, no errors), `ts-travel-service`, `ts-route-service`, `ts-seat-service`, and the other services.

The user-facing degradation is the `travelPlan` endpoints (cheapest, minStation, quickest). The `ui-dashboard` latency is the visible symptom of those timeouts.

### Root cause
- `ts-route-plan-service` makes two outbound POSTs per request. One goes to `ts-travel-service` and returns in about 5 ms. The other goes to `ts-travel2-service` (`/trips/left` or `/trips/routes`) and hangs for about 130 s with no response code.
